newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Korea Electric goes limit-up.
newsitem.headline: Korea Electric goes limit-up.

text.p: Shares in Korea Electric Power Corp rose to their upper limit in Wednesday's active morning trade after Tuesday's announcement that the foreign shareholding ceiling would be raised next month, brokers said.
The shares rose 1,400 won to their limit of 25,800 on heavy volume.
Brokers said KEPCO was in demand because it was viewed as having stable earnings prospects, with captive domestic users.

"People like KEPCO because it's a utility and so it's earnings are seen as very stable and safe," said a UBS Securities broker. Many export-oriented blue chips have been battered by worsening trade conditions.
Foreigners are currently paying around 16 percent in over-the-counter premiums for KEPCO shares.
The finance ministry said foreign holdings in KEPCO and other government-controlled companies will be boosted to 15 percent from the current 12 percent from October 1.
The combined foreign shareholding ceiling for private firms will also be raised to 20 percent from the current 18 percent.
Brokers said the limit expansion is expected to bring some $1.5 billion into the Seoul market.
